chunks: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from al-Hasan ibn Malik, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام about a man who married his daughter to another man, then desired him, but later lost interest in him after that and wished to separate him from his daughter. But the son-in-law refused that and did not respond to divorce, so he pressed him regarding the dowry of his daughter so that he would respond to divorce, while the father's aim was to free her from him. So when he was pressed regarding the dowry, he agreed to the divorce.
So he عليه السلام wrote: 'If the disinterest is from the standpoint of religion, then let him proceed to seek release. But if it is otherwise, then he should not involve himself in that.'

key_terms.التَّخَلُّصِ: seeking release or removal from the marriage situation
key_terms.الدِّينِ: religious grounds or considerations of religion
key_terms.الزُّهْدُ: loss of desire or disinterest toward the son-in-law
key_terms.مَهْرِ: the dowry owed in the marriage

ai.seo_question: Can a father seek to separate his daughter from her husband if he later dislikes the marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses whether a father may intervene to separate his daughter from her husband by leveraging the dowry issue. The ruling distinguishes between a religiously grounded concern, in which case seeking separation is permitted, and other motives, in which case interference is not allowed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4500 - Abdullah ibn Jafar al-Himyari narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Malik, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (as) about a man who had married his daughter to another man. Initially, he was pleased with him, but later he lost interest in him and wished to separate his daughter from him.
However, the son-in-law refused to comply and did not agree to divorce her. The father then demanded the dowry of his daughter from him to compel him to agree to the divorce. The father's intention was to free his daughter from the marriage. When the dowry was demanded, the son-in-law agreed to the divorce.

Imam (as) wrote in reply: "If the disinterest is based on religious grounds, then let him seek to free himself from the situation. However, if it is for any other reason, he should not interfere in the matter."
